steps.text: I'm June, Maya's aunt. Her birthday is this week and I want to give her $300. Should I just send her the cash? She's on SSI, and her family made a Giftwise page for her: maya.

Gift page for Maya (/g/maya). Open needs: Wheelchair repair: $420 still needed, paid to Riverside Mobility Repair; Laptop for college: $649 still needed, paid to Eastgate College Bookstore; Electric bill, this month: $138 still needed, paid to Maya's ABLE account; Therapy co-pay: $90 still needed, paid to Northside Physical Therapy. Any amount can also go to her ABLE account.

Cash counts as income. $300 minus $80 in exclusions leaves $220 counted in November, so their January check would be $774. Giving the item itself keeps $994. Sources: 20 CFR 416.1121: types of unearned income, including gifts; POMS SI 00830.520: Gifts; POMS SI 00810.410: Infrequent or Irregular Income Exclusion; POMS SI 00810.420: $20 General Income Exclusion; POMS SI 02005.001: Retrospective monthly accounting.
$300 for Maya: $300 to Riverside Mobility Repair (Wheelchair repair). Her check stays $994. Given as cash, it would be $774.

June, I'd hold off on sending cash. That's a kind gift, but SSI would count it against Maya's check.

**If you send $300 cash:** Social Security counts $220 of it as income, after $80 that doesn't count. Her monthly check for January would go from $994 to $774, so she'd lose $220. None of that money goes to Social Security; she just gets a smaller check.

**What I'd suggest:** Maya's Giftwise page lists a wheelchair repair that still needs $420. Giftwise would send your full $300 straight to Riverside Mobility Repair for it. A payment made directly to a shop for something that isn't housing doesn't count against her, so her January check stays at $994.

Other needs on her page include a laptop for college, a therapy co-pay and her ABLE account (a savings account for people with disabilities). The wheelchair repair is where Giftwise sends your $300.

Would you like me to set this up? If you say yes, I'll make a PayPal checkout and send you the link. Nothing is charged until you approve it in PayPal yourself.
That makes sense. Yes, please set up the $300 that way.

PayPal checkout ready for $300 to Maya, paid to 1 recipient. The person giving should open this link and approve in PayPal: [PayPal approval link]. After they approve, the receipt will be at /r/[receipt].

June, your $300 gift for Maya is ready for you to approve. PayPal's own record shows one payment of $300 for Maya's wheelchair repair, and it's waiting for you to approve it.

Approve it here: [PayPal approval link]

This is a PayPal test version, so no real money will move, even after you approve.

If you'd sent the $300 as cash, Maya's check for January would have gone from $994 to $774. Paid straight to the repair shop, it stays at $994.

After you approve, your receipt will be here: /r/[receipt]

What a lovely birthday gift for Maya.
